loading.tips.architecture: Want architecture checks too? Turn on **Clean Architecture** and **DDD** with their star in Standards.
loading.tips.assistant: Press **Ctrl+`** to open the assistant, then ask it why a score is low.
loading.tips.cancelKeep: Cancelling a run? Choose **Keep findings** and the work done so far still gets scored.
loading.tips.cleanScan: Changed your standards or refactored a lot? Turn on **Clean scan** to re‑check every file.
loading.tips.compliance: Quodeq also counts what your code does right. **Good practices raise a score**, never lower it.
loading.tips.customStandard: Need your own rules? **Any chat AI can write a custom standard** for you. Help shows how.
loading.tips.dismiss: False positive? **Dismiss it** with a reason. It stays dismissed unless the file moves.
loading.tips.dismissByType: Same false positive everywhere? A finding's ⋯ menu **dismisses every instance of its rule** at once.
loading.tips.duel: Put any two projects side by side with the **duel** button on Compare.
loading.tips.exportZip: No shared repository? **Export a project as a .zip** and import it on another machine, history included.
loading.tips.fetchLatest: Before re‑evaluating a cloned project, its row's ⋯ menu **fetches the latest code**.
loading.tips.fixplans: Stuck on a finding? **Fix plan** gives you step‑by‑step instructions to paste into your AI assistant.
loading.tips.githubSignIn: Private repo won't clone? In Settings, **sign in with GitHub** and approve a short code in your browser.
loading.tips.ignore: Keep generated or third‑party code out of your score with a `.quodeqignore` file.
loading.tips.incremental: Re‑runs are quick: **only files that changed** since the last run get checked again.
loading.tips.matrix: On Compare, **click a column header** in the score table to rank your projects by it.
loading.tips.monorepo: Working in a monorepo? Set **Scope** to a subfolder and each package becomes its own project.
loading.tips.ollama: Private code? Use **Ollama** and the analysis runs entirely on your machine.
loading.tips.prReview: Run `quodeq review` on a branch to post its findings on the pull request.
loading.tips.reviewDryRun: Add `--dry-run` to `quodeq review` to **preview the comments** before anything gets posted.
loading.tips.riskTab: Not sure where to start? On the Map's **Risk** tab, the areas near the centre need rework first.
loading.tips.sarif: In CI, `--sarif` writes findings that **GitHub code scanning** can show.
loading.tips.shareAssistant: Remote projects are read‑only, but **the assistant still explains** their scores and findings.
loading.tips.shareBareRepo: No GitHub needed: a local `git init --bare` folder **works as an evaluations repository**.
loading.tips.shareCompare: Published projects join Compare too, so you can **duel yours against anyone's**.
loading.tips.shareDisconnect: Disconnecting the evaluations repository **only deletes your local copy**. Nothing you published is touched.
loading.tips.shareInvite: Inviting someone? On Repositories, **copy invite** gives them a message they only need to paste.
loading.tips.shareLocation: The **location** filter on Repositories shows what lives only on your machine and is not shared yet.
loading.tips.sharePublishedBy: Others see **published by** with your git `user.name`, so set it before your first publish.
loading.tips.sharePullCopy: Want to re‑evaluate a remote project? **pull local copy** brings it over with its full history.
loading.tips.shareSecondMachine: Add the same evaluations repository on another machine and **every published project shows up**, no scan needed.
loading.tips.shareStandards: Connected an evaluations repository? **Share your custom standards** from the Sync column in Standards.
loading.tips.shareUpdate: Finished a new run? Press **update** on the project's row to publish it.
loading.tips.shared: **Publish evaluations to any git repository** and browse them from every machine. Start on Repositories.
loading.tips.stale: On Compare, a **stale** grade means the code changed since its last run, not that the run is old.
loading.tips.standards: Changed a threshold? It is kept **on this machine, per project**. The repository is never written.
loading.tips.testAccess: Clone failing? Quodeq **shows why** and offers ways forward, such as signing in with GitHub.
loading.tips.timeLimit: Hit the time limit? Finished work is scored and **the next run picks up the remaining files**.
loading.tips.trustModel: Service only listens locally? Commit `.quodeq/project-profile.json` so **exposure findings match how you deploy**.
loading.tips.warmup: After an update, Quodeq **recalculates grades in the background**, newest projects first.

settings.effortDesc: How hard the model thinks about each file. Default leaves it to the CLI.
settings.effortHint: Higher effort finds more but runs slower and uses more of your plan or credits. Results are cached per effort, so after a change the next evaluation analyses every file again.
settings.gradeFormulaDesc: Tune how violations and compliance turn into grades. Changes rescore all runs.
settings.installGeneric: Install this provider on your machine and restart Quodeq, and this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintClaude: Install Claude Code from Anthropic's official documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `claude` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintCodex: Install the OpenAI Codex CLI from the official OpenAI documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `codex` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintCopilot: Install GitHub Copilot CLI with `npm install -g @github/copilot`, then restart Quodeq. Sign in using the dedicated Quodeq profile described in the provider help.
settings.copilotSetup: Copilot uses a separate Quodeq profile. Sign in once on macOS/Linux: `COPILOT_HOME="$HOME/.quodeq/copilot" copilot login`. In PowerShell, set `$env:COPILOT_HOME="$HOME/.quodeq/copilot"` before running `copilot login`. Keep this profile free of plugins and custom MCP servers. Your account's model access, usage limits and company policies still apply.
settings.copilotModelsInvalid: Copilot returned no usable model list.
settings.installHintGemini: Install the Gemini CLI from Google's official documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `gemini` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintAgy: Install Google's Antigravity CLI from its official documentation and sign in by running `agy` once, then restart Quodeq. Once `agy` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.liveFindingsDesc: While a scan is running, show only the findings it produces. Findings reused from unchanged files stay in the final report either way.
settings.llamacppLoadFailed: We couldn't reach llama-server. Make sure it is running on port 8080.
settings.llamacppModelHintP1: llama-server runs one model at a time, fixed at launch by the `-m` flag. Whatever you started it with is what shows up here.
settings.llamacppModelHintP2: To switch models, stop llama-server and relaunch it with a different GGUF file. For speculative decoding (MTP), pair the target model with a smaller drafter via `--model-draft`.
settings.llamacppNoModel: No model loaded yet. Start llama-server with a GGUF file.
settings.llamacppOffline: llama-server isn't running. Start it with `llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080`.

settings.loadedModelDesc: The GGUF currently loaded by llama-server.
settings.localApiModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your {provider} models. Make sure {provider} is running.
settings.localServerHint: This server runs entirely on your own machine, so nothing leaves your computer. Quodeq is a local-first app that respects your privacy.
settings.menubarToggleDesc: Keep Quodeq in the menu bar to monitor, start, and stop the dashboard, even when this window is closed.
settings.menubarToggleFailed: Could not update the menu bar setting. Try again.
settings.modeDesc: Choose light, dark, or follow your system
settings.modelHintClaude: The list comes from Claude Code and shows the models your account can use. `opus`, `sonnet` and `haiku` always follow the latest version; the dated ids under Specific versions stay fixed. For an id that is not listed, choose Other model id. Press ↻ after a new release.
settings.modelHintCodex: The list comes from Codex and shows the models your account can use; the recommended one is the Codex default. For an id that is not listed, choose Other model id. Press ↻ after a new release.
settings.modelHintCopilot: Choose Auto or a model available to your signed-in Copilot account. The list is loaded through your dedicated Quodeq profile.
settings.modelHintGemini: Run `gemini` and type `/model` to see the models your account can use, then copy the id here, for example `gemini-2.5-pro` or `gemini-2.5-flash`.
settings.modelHintAgy: The list comes from `agy models` and shows the models your Google account can use. The last part of a Gemini id, such as `high` or `low`, is its thinking level.
settings.modelSourceDesc: Default follows your evaluation provider and model. Choose Custom to pick a different one for the assistant.
settings.modelsUnavailable: Could not list the models. Type a model id, or press ↻ to try again.
settings.needModelBeforeEval: You'll need a model before you can run an evaluation.
settings.ollamaModelHint: This list comes straight from your local Ollama server. To add a model, download it with Ollama itself (for example, `ollama pull gemma4:26b`). As soon as the download finishes, it shows up here.
settings.ollamaModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your Ollama models. Make sure Ollama is running.
settings.ollamaOffline: Ollama isn't running. Start it with `ollama serve`, or open the Ollama app.
settings.ollamaSubagentsDesc: Starts at 1. Auto-detect measures what your hardware can serve.
settings.omlxModelHint: This list comes from your local omlx server. To add a model, use the omlx admin UI at `http://localhost:8000/admin` or pull a model with the omlx CLI. Models show up here as soon as they are downloaded.
settings.omlxModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your omlx models. Make sure omlx is running.

settings.omlxSubagentsDesc: We make a guess based on your unified memory. Run a quick test for a more accurate number.

settings.pickModelToStart: Pick a model to get started.
settings.pickModelYouWant: Pick the model you want to use.
settings.providerHintP1: Quodeq works with several AI providers, but you need to install each one before you can use it.
settings.providerHintP2: For the CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity), install them on your machine and they show up here ready to go. Ollama needs to be running locally. Cloud providers like OpenRouter need an API key, which you paste in their tab.
settings.providerHintP3: Greyed out tabs below mean that provider isn't installed yet.
settings.providerRunsDesc: Choose which AI runs your evaluations.
settings.providersLoadFailed: We couldn't load your AI providers. Make sure the server is running.
settings.restartDesc: Stop the server with `Ctrl+C` in the terminal, then run `quodeq dashboard` to restart. This page will reconnect automatically.
settings.restartTerminalConfirmMessage: This kills every open terminal session. Any running commands will be interrupted.
settings.showWelcomeDesc: Open the welcome and the first-run steps again, even if you skipped them before. Your projects and settings stay as they are.
settings.groupAboutDesc: Version, updates, the welcome and links.
settings.groupAppDesc: How quodeq looks and which tools sit in the toolbar.
settings.groupAssistantDesc: Which model answers in the assistant.
settings.groupConnectionsDesc: Your GitHub account, the repository you share evaluations through, and the local server.
settings.groupEvaluationDesc: Which AI reads your code, how long it may take, and how findings become grades.
settings.githubUsingGh: Using your gh login. quodeq will clone with it.
settings.githubNotSignedIn: Not signed in. quodeq uses your git setup.
settings.githubExpired: Signed in as {login}, but the token expired. Sign in again.
settings.sharedSnippetsDesc: Publish the code each finding points at. Off: findings keep their file, line and reason, but the code stays on this machine.
settings.subagentsDescRemote: How many subagents work side by side. Pick a number from 1 to 10.
settings.subagentsHintOllamaP1: Quodeq splits an evaluation into separate checks (one for each quality dimension) and runs them at the same time. More subagents means a faster run, but it also uses more memory at once.
settings.subagentsHintOllamaP2: Your VRAM sets the real ceiling here. Use Auto-detect to let Quodeq pick a safe default, or run a quick test to see what your hardware can comfortably handle.
settings.subagentsHintRemoteP1: Quodeq splits an evaluation into separate checks (one for each quality dimension) and runs them at the same time. More subagents means a faster run, but it also means more requests in flight.
settings.subagentsHintRemoteP2: Your AI provider sets its own concurrency limits, so the number you pick here is the most Quodeq will try to run at once. The provider may queue or throttle some of them.
settings.terminalEnableDesc: Shows a shell (❯_) in the toolbar drawer. Ctrl+Shift+` opens it. Localhost only; on by default.
settings.terminalRestartDesc: Every terminal session starts in your home directory. Restart closes them all and opens a fresh one.
settings.thisModelEveryStep: This model handles every step of your evaluation.
settings.timeLimitDesc: Stop the evaluation after this long. You'll still see whatever finished in time, and the next run continues from there.
settings.timeLimitHintBase: Most of the token usage happens during the analysis phase, so this is your main way to keep a run short. Whatever finished in time still shows up in your results, and the next evaluation picks up from where this one stopped instead of starting over.
settings.timeLimitHintCloud: Heads up: a cloud evaluation runs against your own provider plan. The longer it runs, the more tokens you'll use. On a long codebase that can add up fast, so keep an eye on your usage and start with a tighter limit if you're not sure.
